hero.title:
Anthropology, excavated
layer by layer.
hero.lead: A mentorship-led preparation system for Anthropology optional — built around the way the subject actually works: fossils, fieldwork, and theory, stratified into a syllabus you can master in order.

strata.title: Homo sapiens
strata.body: Modern cognition, symbolic behaviour, global dispersal. The reference point for every comparison question Paper I asks.

strata.title: Homo erectus
strata.body: First controlled use of fire, first hominin to leave Africa, Acheulian tool tradition — a favourite for archaeological-anthropology questions.

strata.title: Homo habilis
strata.body: "Handy man" — the Oldowan toolkit and the formal beginning of the archaeological record examiners keep returning to.

strata.title: Australopithecus afarensis
strata.body: Bipedal, small-brained — "Lucy" is the single most-cited fossil in Paper I evolution answers.

strata.title: Sahelanthropus & the hominin split
strata.body: Where the primate lineage and the hominin lineage diverge — the opening argument of every primatology answer.

paper1.title: Primates & the Living Record
items: Living major primates & their conservation status

paper1.title: Human Evolution & Variation
items: Fossil evidence: Australopithecines to Homo sapiens

paper1.title: Prehistory & Material Culture
items: Tool typology & technology through the ages

paper2.label: Entry 01 — Prehistoric & Ethnic Foundations
paper2.title: The Peopling of India
paper2.body: Paleolithic to Neolithic cultures on the subcontinent, and the racial and linguistic classifications historically used to describe Indian populations.

paper2.label: Entry 02 — Social Structure
paper2.title: Caste, Tribe & Village India
paper2.body: The structural and cultural dimensions of Indian society: varna and jati, tribe-caste continuum, and the village as a unit of study.

paper2.label: Entry 03 — Tribal Situation
paper2.title: Scheduled Tribes & Development
paper2.body: Classification of Indian tribes by region and economy, the impact of urbanisation and industrialisation, and constitutional safeguards.

paper2.label: Entry 04 — Applied & Contemporary
paper2.title: Anthropology in Policy
paper2.body: Applied anthropology in tribal welfare, health, and national development planning — where the paper meets current governance debates.

paper2.label: Entry 05 — Religion & Belief Systems
paper2.title: Tribal & Folk Religion
paper2.body: Religious pluralism in India, tribal belief systems, and the process of sanskritisation and religious syncretism.

phases.title: Foundation Layer
phases.body: Topic-wise tests on each unit of Paper I and Paper II, taken right after that unit is taught. Builds recall before it builds speed.

phases.title: Sedimentary Layer
phases.body: Full-syllabus questions mixed across units, forcing you to connect theory with case material — exactly how UPSC frames real questions.

phases.title: Compression Layer
phases.body: Full-length, three-hour simulated Mains papers under exam conditions, with the same time pressure and question count as the real exam.

phases.title: Surface Layer
phases.body: Final revision tests built entirely from your own past mistakes and weak topics, taken in the last six weeks before the exam.

included.title: Line-by-line evaluation
included.body: Margin notes on structure, content and missed keywords, not just a number.

included.title: Model answer booklet
included.body: A model answer for every question, written within the actual word/time limit.

included.title: Diagram bank
included.body: Ready-to-reproduce diagrams for evolution, kinship and settlement-pattern questions.

included.title: Rank-list benchmarking
included.body: See where your score falls against the batch after every full-length test.

included.title: One-on-one review call
included.body: A short call after every full-length test to walk through what to fix next.

included.title: Current affairs linkage
included.body: Monthly notes connecting tribal affairs and policy news back to Paper II topics.

testimonials.quote: The core-sample way of teaching evolution finally made the fossil sequence stick — I stopped mixing up habilis and erectus in the exam hall.
Weekly answer evaluation was the single biggest jump in my score between the first and third full-length test.
Having one mentor track my Paper II answers meant feedback actually built on itself, cycle after cycle.
